title: The statutory recovery and monitoring program: who may enter, who decides, and what admission does to a pending matter
rule_summary: M.G.L. c. 112, § 65G(b)(1) requires the department of public health to establish a voluntary program for monitoring the rehabilitation of licensed health care professionals who seek support for their mental health or substance use or who are referred to the program by a licensing board; § 65G was inserted by St. 2022, c. 177, § 36. Under § 65G(a) a licensed health care professional is an individual who holds a license, a license is a license, registration, authorization or certificate issued by a board of registration, and a licensing board is a board of registration that has issued a license; boards of registration include those serving in the department under M.G.L. c. 13, § 9, other than the board of registration established under c. 13, § 10, and M.G.L. c. 13, § 9(a) names the board of registration in pharmacy among the boards serving in the department of public health. Under § 65G(e) the department employs a program director who shall admit eligible licensed health care professionals who request to participate, provide each participant with a written individualized rehabilitation plan with requirements for supervision and surveillance, and terminate a participant based on noncompliance with that plan or material misrepresentations concerning the participant's participation in the program or professional practice; any restriction or condition relating to a participant's professional practice required under § 65G(e), and any change to one, is subject to the approval of the participant's licensing board. Under § 65G(d)(2) a rehabilitation evaluation committee appointed by the commissioner evaluates licensed health care professionals who request to participate within 5 business days of receipt of the request and provides recommendations regarding admission, and makes recommendations on whether a participant may continue or resume professional practice within the full scope of the license and on an individualized rehabilitation plan. Under § 65G(f) a licensed health care professional who applies to participate in or is referred by the licensing board to the program shall specify, in a form and format set by the department, the mental health condition or substance use that they believe may impede or has affected their ability to safely practice their profession, and shall agree to comply, to the best of their ability, with an individualized rehabilitation plan to be admitted; noncompliance with the plan may result in termination from the program only if the plan states that noncompliance will result in termination. Under § 65G(g), upon admission the licensing board may dismiss any pending investigation or complaint against the participant that arises from or relates to the participant's mental health or substance use, may change the participant's publicly-available license status to reflect the existence of non-disciplinary restrictions or conditions, and may immediately suspend the participant's license as is necessary to protect the public health, safety and welfare upon receipt of notice from the director that the participant has withdrawn from the program before completion or that the director has terminated the participant from the program.
exam_relevance: Tests the two routes into the program, the division of decisions between the department's program and the licensing board, the discretionary and limited effect of admission on a pending matter, and the licensing board's power to suspend immediately on withdrawal or termination.

numeric_facts.fact: rehabilitation evaluation committee evaluation of a request to participate

exceptions: Noncompliance with an individualized rehabilitation plan may result in termination only if the plan states that noncompliance will result in termination
common_confusions: Admission does not itself dismiss a pending investigation or complaint; the licensing board may dismiss one that arises from or relates to the participant's mental health or substance use.

The department runs the program through its director and a rehabilitation evaluation committee, while dismissal, public license status, suspension and the approval of practice restrictions rest with the licensing board.
The program is open both to a professional who seeks support and to one referred by a licensing board.
verification_notes: Read on 2026-09-16 in the current text of M.G.L. c. 112, § 65G and M.G.L. c. 13, § 9 on malegislature.gov, and in St. 2022, c. 177, § 36, which inserted § 65G.
